current_bottleneck: The exact shared-state/shared-randomness joint IV+anchor AR route is now implemented and mechanically viable, but the 2-epoch smoke is undertrained and not deployable. last_result_summary: 609a implemented a generic 510a-style empirical-score AR transition flow over arbitrary state panels: D=25 for IV-only or D=38 for IV+13 anchor states. Focused tests passed (2 passed). A joint38 smoke trained for 2 epochs on 512 recent windows, with val loss improving 0.930->0.868 and finite joint samples. Official IV bridge on 128 windows/24 samples scored 3/11: surface, block-AR, and cross-cell correlation passed; coverage, conditionality, time-series, cointegration, regime coverage, distributional fidelity, mean reversion, and pathwise jump realism failed. Key metrics: cov90 83.2%, conditional MAE reduction 3.1%, turb/calm width ratio 0.906, daily KS 21/25, level KS 6/25, corr/rank 0.630/2.965, h30 mean-reversion ratio 0.913 but h1 ratio 0.665, path max-jump KS 0.891.
next_step_recommendation: Continue within the 609-family. Run a stronger joint38 AR training run with more epochs and more recent windows before adding architecture knobs. The next falsifier should determine whether the exact hybrid can recover the structural frontier when trained beyond smoke scale.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11. On the 441-window broad frame, 510a and 596a both score 5/11, but 510a is the better risk profile because 596a narrows coverage and worsens distributional fidelity. 574a remains the best risk-manager joint stress product but is a composed deck, not a calibrated joint law. 609a creates the missing native shared-state joint AR route and should be scaled before judging the paradigm.
